Plot paired Alert System pathway responses

AlertHeatmap.Rd

Pathways are selected independently on the positive and negative sides using an evidence-aware priority metric. Tile color displays either the raw paired pathway effect or its null-standardized value. Text annotations display response prevalence (r) and directional consistency (c).

Usage

AlertHeatmap(
  seurat_obj,
  misc_name = "AlertSystem",
  score_method = c("expression", "ucell"),
  top_n = 5L,
  side = c("both", "positive", "negative"),
  select_by = c("widespread_priority", "focal_priority", "abs_effect", "null_z",
    "robust_fraction", "response_rate"),
  fill_by = c("effect", "null_z"),
  reorder_by = c("effect", "select"),
  scale_mode = c("none", "unit"),
  unit_q = 0.9,
  show_annotations = TRUE,
  show_fdr = TRUE,
  fdr_cutoff = 0.05,
  fill_limits = NULL
)

Arguments

seurat_obj

Seurat object processed by AlertSystemScore().

misc_name

Name of the Alert System state in seurat_obj@misc.

score_method

Score channel: "expression" or "ucell".

top_n

Number of pathways selected separately from each requested effect side.

side

One of "both", "positive", or "negative".

select_by

Ranking metric: "widespread_priority", "focal_priority", "abs_effect", "null_z", "robust_fraction", or "response_rate".

fill_by

Tile fill: raw "effect" or calibrated "null_z".

reorder_by

Order selected pathways by mean effect or selection score.

scale_mode

"none" retains the native response scale; "unit" divides by a robust magnitude and clips display values to [-1, 1].

unit_q

Quantile of absolute displayed values used by unit scaling.

show_annotations

Display r and c in each tile.

show_fdr

Display * when FDR is at or below fdr_cutoff.

fdr_cutoff

FDR threshold for the symbol.

fill_limits

Optional explicit symmetric or asymmetric fill limits.

Value

A ggplot object. Selection data and display metadata are attached as attributes: selected_pathways, selection_stats, change_measure, response_threshold, and fill_limits.

Details

UPDATED: UCell difference and UCell log2-ratio results are labeled explicitly, and mixed transformations are rejected rather than silently plotted together.
